The package defines a postinstall script that runs install.js, and install.js contains an obfuscated base64 payload that is decoded and executed via new Function("require", decoded). The decoded logic (visible in the payload fragments) collects system details (platform, release, arch, hostname, username, homedir, network interfaces, nodeVersion, cwd, execPath, etc.) and builds HTTPS request options with obfuscated hostnames — then sends that data off-host. Automatic execution of obfuscated code at install time that harvests system metadata and exfiltrates it is a classic malicious supply-chain/backdoor behavior. The lack of repository/author metadata increases the risk.

The file decodes a large base64 blob and immediately executes it via new Function("require", decoded); r(require) — a classic dynamic-eval/loader pattern used to hide behavior. The decoded payload references require('os') and many system properties (platform, release, hostname, homedir, network interfaces, execPath) and builds an HTTPS URL, indicating system fingerprinting and likely remote payload download/exfiltration. Combined obfuscation, runtime code-generation, passing require into the generated function, and network-related behavior are strong indicators of deliberate malicious activity.
